guest_hosts.credential_frame: A composite of multi-year Framework owners who migrated from ThinkPads and have documented the transition honestly — including the parts that didn't work as advertised
guest_hosts.delivery_baseline: Measured, slightly dry. Speaks in short declarative sentences. Pauses before answering. Not warm, not cold — just honest.
guest_hosts.expertise: What the Framework ownership experience actually costs in attention over time — the expansion card shuffle, the keyboard adjustment period, the community dependency, and whether the mainboard upgrade path feels like a real option or a theoretical one
guest_hosts.label: MAREN
guest_hosts.personality: Pragmatic and slightly impatient with ideology. Bought the Framework because the argument was sound, not because she was a fan. Will say 'it's fine' about things that are genuinely fine and 'that's real friction' about things that aren't. Doesn't perform enthusiasm.
guest_hosts.role_in_episode: Enters after Caspar lays out the repairability convergence. Complicates the Framework side of the ledger by naming the ownership tax — the things you have to think about that a ThinkPad user never does. Exits before the recommendation logic so Juno and Caspar can close without her framing dominating.

key_claims.claim: ThinkPad X1 Carbon Gen 14 scored 9/10 from iFixit for repairability—the highest score ever for a mainstream ultralight laptop. Battery, SSD, keyboard, USB-C ports, and fans are all user-replaceable.
ThinkPad X1 Carbon Gen 14 weighs 996g (2.15 lbs) with OLED display, making it the lightest laptop in its performance class. The IPS version weighs 1.14kg.
Framework 13 Pro battery life: 20 hours claimed (Netflix streaming at 250 nits), 12-16 hours real-world mixed workload. Previous Framework 13 AMD models got only 4-5 hours under coding workloads.
ThinkPad X1 Carbon Gen 14 battery life: up to 24 hours in WiFi test (IPS display), 14 hours at full brightness. OLED versions get significantly less.
Framework 13 Pro AMD configurations start around $2,500 for comparable specs (HX 370, 32GB RAM, 1TB SSD). ThinkPad X1 Carbon Gen 14 starts at $1,999, typically configured around $2,500-2,800.
ThinkPad X1 Carbon Gen 14 has soldered RAM (32GB or 64GB, no upgrades). Framework 13 Pro uses LPCAMM2 (Intel) or SO-DIMM (AMD), upgradeable to 64GB.
Framework confirmed Ubuntu configurations are outselling Windows on the 13 Pro—unusual for any laptop manufacturer.
Framework has raised $40M total across 4 funding rounds. In July 2026, the CEO warned that supplier costs put the company at 'financial risk.'
ThinkPad X1 Carbon series has sold over 10 million units since 2012. Business users report reliable operation after 5-6 years of daily use.
Framework 13 Pro keyboard rated 'B+' by PCWorld, below Lenovo and Microsoft but improved from previous generations.
